rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'fa-idhā hum mubṣirūn,' idhā marks sudden discovery, while idhā in 'when something touches them' introduces a condition that calls for a consequence.
rows.anchor: معنى { إذا } ههنا للمفاجأة ، كقولك خرجت فإذا زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent reading takes their brothers as human devils, who mislead people and thereby assist the jinn devils in misguidance.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : وهو الأظهر أن المعنى : وإخوان الشياطين يمدون الشياطين في الغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the brothers the non-pious people whom devils support in error; both readings assume every disbeliever has a devil brother.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن إخوان الشياطين هم الناس الذين ليسوا بمتقين ، فإن الشياطين يكونون مددا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils' support consists of strengthening the whispering, persisting in it, and distracting the person from recognizing its ugliness and faults.
rows.anchor: تفسير الإمداد تقوية تلك الوسوسة والإقامة عليها وشغل النفس عن الوقوف على قبائحها ومعايبها

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads yudiddūnahum with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on mīm; the other readers use the form with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on mīm.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : قرأ نافع { يمدونهم } ( بضم الياء وكسر الميم من الإمداد ، والباقون { يمدونهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One lexical distinction says madda means to pull or draw, whereas amadda means to provide additional aid.
rows.anchor: وقيل مد معناه جذب ، وأمد معناه من الإمداد .

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the Qur'an generally uses amadda for commendable provision (23:55; 52:22; 27:36), but madda for its opposite, as in 2:15.
rows.anchor: / قال الواحدي ، عامة ما جاء في التنزيل مما يحمد ويستحب أمددت على أفعلت ، كقوله : { أنما نمدهم به من مال وبنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading with ḍamma, a normally positive form is used for its opposite, as when glad tidings are announced of painful punishment; the common reading is with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: ومن ضم الياء استعمل ما هو الخير لضده كقوله : { فبشرهم بعذاب أليم }

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines iqṣār as refraining from or stopping something.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : الإقصار الكف عن الشيء

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd says a person 'aqṣara' when he stops and desists from evil.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد : أقصر فلان عن الشر يقصر إقصارا إذا كف عنه وانتهى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that the deviant does not stop going astray and the one leading others astray does not stop leading them astray.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ثم لا يقصرون عن الضلال والإضلال ، أما الغاوي ففي الضلال وأما المغوي ففي الإضلال .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After declaring the Qur'an clear proofs, guidance, and mercy, God follows by commanding listeners to hear it and be silent.
rows.anchor: لما عظم شأن القرآن بقوله : { هاذا بصائر من ربكم } ( الأعراف : 203 ) أردفه بقوله : { وإذا قرىء القرءان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inṣāt means silence; naṣata, anṣata, and intaṣata are used with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: الإنصات السكوت والاستماع ، يقال : نصت ، وأنصت ، وانتصت ، بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is phrased as a command, whose apparent force is obligation, so listening and silence appear obligatory; scholars differ over its scope.
rows.anchor: لا شك أن قوله : { فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا } أمره ، وظاهر الأمر للوجوب

rows.speaker: الحسن وأهل الظاهر
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and the literalists apply the command generally: whenever anyone recites Qur'an, everyone must listen silently, including passersby and children's teachers.
rows.anchor: القول الأول : وهو قول الحسن وقول أهل الظاهر أنا نجري هذه الآية على عمومها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that people used to talk during prayer, so this verse was revealed commanding silence.
rows.anchor: قال أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه : كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت هذه الآية ، وأمروا بالإنصات

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says people in prayer talked about their needs and answered arrivals asking how much they had prayed or how much remained; the verse was revealed about this.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : كان الرجل يأتي وهم في الصلاة فيسألهم ، كم صليتم وكم بقي ؟

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet and companions recited aloud in obligatory prayer, confusing one another, and the verse then came down.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الصلاة المكتوبة وقرأ أصحابه وراءه رافعين أصواتهم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions take the verse to prohibit followers from reciting aloud behind the imam.
rows.anchor: فخلطوا عليه ، فنزلت هذه الآية وهو قول أبي حنيفة وأصحابه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء والشافعي
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ, with this view also transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī, understand the verse as requiring silence during the sermon.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وعطاء وهذا القول منقول عن الشافعي رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī finds restricting the verse to the sermon highly unlikely: idhā connects an event to its consequence but does not imply repetition, as in a one-time conditional divorce.
rows.anchor: وأقول هذا القول في غاية البعد لأن لفظة إذا تفيد الارتباط ، ولا تفيد التكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since idhā does not entail repetition, one occasion of Qur'an recitation fulfills the command; the sermon reading suffices, leaving no further indication in the wording.
rows.anchor: قوله : { وإذا قرىء القرءان فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا } لا يفيد إلا وجوب الإنصات مرة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Shāfiʿī's position the imam pauses so the follower may recite al-Fātiḥa; Abū Salama says the imam has two pauses in which one may seize an opportunity to recite.
rows.anchor: عند الشافعي رحمه الله : يسكت الإمام ، وحينئذ يقرأ المأموم الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects the pause defense: if the imam's pause is obligatory it lacks consensus, and if optional the imam may recite while the follower does, violating listening; the duration may be too short and makes the imam subordinate.
rows.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : سكوت الإمام إما أن نقول : إنه من الواجبات أو ليس من الواجبات والأول باطل بالإجماع

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī proposes that inṣāt means refraining from speaking aloud, so Arabs can call a silent reader who cannot be heard anṣat.
rows.anchor: وذكر الواحدي سؤالا ثانيا على التمسك بالآية . فقال : إن الإنصات هو ترك الجهر والعرب تسمي تارك الجهر منصتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī replies that reciting, even silently, prevents listening: listening means full attention, as in God's command to Moses, so the command to listen entails a ban on recitation.
rows.anchor: فالاستماع عبارة عن كونه بحيث يحيط بذلك الكلام المسموع على الوجه الكامل ، قال تعالى لموسى عليه السلام : { وأنا اخترتك فاستمع لما يوحى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī calls it sound that jurists allow Qur'an's general wording to be specified by a solitary report: the specific hadith requiring al-Fātiḥa in prayer limits this verse's general command.
rows.anchor: الفقهاء أجمعوا على أنه يجوز تخصيص عموم القرآن / بخبر الواحد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's reports say there is no prayer for one who has not recited the Opening and no prayer except with the Opening; Rāzī treats them as more specific than the verse.
rows.anchor: إلا أن قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب ) وقوله : ( لا صلاة إلا بفاتحة الكتاب )

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي في قوله القديم
rows.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī in his earlier position bar followers from reciting al-Fātiḥa in audible prayers, based on this text, but require it in silent prayers, which the verse does not address.
rows.anchor: مذهب مالك وهو القول القديم للشافعي أنه لا يجوز للمأموم أن يقرأ الفاتحة في الصلوات الجهرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī's fifth view addresses disbelievers at the start of revelation; applying the verse to followers behind an imam would sever its link to the preceding discussion of demands for signs and the Qur'an's sufficiency.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية قول خامس وهو أن قوله تعالى : { وإذا قرىء القرءان فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا } خطاب مع الكفار في ابتداء التبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers must listen as the Prophet recites, so they can grasp the Qur'an's eloquence and knowledge, recognize its miraculous proof of his truth, and see why other miracles are unnecessary.
rows.anchor: استمعوا له وأنصتوا حتى يقفوا على فصاحته ، ويحيطوا بما فيه من العلوم الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because disbelievers had said to drown out the Qur'an rather than listen, Rāzī sees the command to listen silently as a fitting response that lets them encounter its inimitability.
rows.anchor: حكى عن الكفار أنهم قالوا : { لا تسمعوا لهاذا القرءان والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون } ( فصلت : 26 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verse definitively calls the Qur'an mercy for believers, so conditional hope of mercy fits disbelievers instead: listening may reveal its signs, lead them to believe, and make them recipients of mercy.
rows.anchor: فحكم تعالى بكون هذا القرآن رحمة للمؤمنين على سبيل القطع والجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī concludes that the audience is disbelievers hearing the Prophet at the start of revelation and the call; this preserves the order and defeats use of the verse for congregational recitation.
rows.anchor: هذا الخطاب ما يتناول المؤمنين ، وإنما تناول الكفار في أول زمان تبليغ الوحي والدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding command to listen presupposes a loud Qur'an reciter, whom Rāzī identifies as the Prophet; after commanding him to proclaim revelation, God turns him to inward remembrance.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أن ذلك القارىء ليس إلا الرسول عليه السلام ، فكانت هذه الآية جارية مجرى أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance in the prescribed inward, humble manner best completes its benefit because it is closer to sincerity and entreaty.
rows.anchor: والفائدة فيه : أن انتفاع الإنسان بالذكر إنما يكمل إذا وقع الذكر بهذه الصفة ، لأنه بهذا الشرط أقرب إلى الأخلاص والتضرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God inwardly means knowing the meanings of spoken invocations and bringing to mind His perfection, might, exaltedness, majesty, and greatness.
rows.anchor: والمراد بذكر الله في نفسه كونه عارفا بمعاني الأذكار التي يقولها بلسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal remembrance without awareness in the heart is fruitless, just as uttering 'I sold' or 'I bought' without understanding those words does not effect a sale.
rows.anchor: الذكر باللسان إذا كان عاريا عن الذكر بالقلب كان عديم الفائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī recounts a spiritual master's method: after forty days of retreat and purification, the disciple hears the ninety-nine names and identifies which most moves the heart; steady repetition of that name may open disclosures.
rows.anchor: سمعت أن بعض الأكابر من أصحاب القلوب كان إذا أراد أن يأمر واحدا من المريدين بالخلوة والذكر

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: The theologians argue that the command to remember God within oneself establishes inward speech, which they identify as inner remembrance.
rows.anchor: قال المتكلمون : هذه الآية تدل على إثبات كلام النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects identifying this remembrance with knowledge: a present concept cannot be sought anew, while what is absent is inconceivable and cannot be sought; commanded inward remembrance must differ from knowledge and conception.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنه لا قدرة للإنسان على تحصيل التصورات ، فامتنع ورود الأمر به ، والآية دالة على ورود الأمر بالذكر النفساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God 'your Lord' here, rather than using another divine name, signals care, nearness, favor, and beneficence, and should make the servant rejoice.
rows.anchor: وإنما سماه في هذا المقام باسم كونه ربا ، وأضاف نفسه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Lord recalls God's innumerable blessings, which human reason cannot encompass, as stated at 14:34; this recognition strengthens hope.
rows.anchor: وعند سماع هذا الاسم يتذكر العبد أقسام نعم الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's name awakens hope and the command to beseech with fear awakens awe; together these motives complete faith, with hope given greater weight by the ordering.
rows.anchor: فلما وقع الابتداء بما يوجب الرجاء ، علمنا أن جانب الرجاء أقوى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying cited by Rāzī says that if a believer's fear and hope were weighed, they would balance one another.
rows.anchor: على ما قال عليه السلام : ( لو وزن خوف المؤمن ورجاؤه لاعتدلا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entreaty is an essential condition of remembrance, supported by the Qur'anic description of people calling on God in distress humbly and privately.
rows.anchor: أما القرآن فقوله في سورة الأنعام { قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه تضرعا وخفية }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human completion requires awareness of divine lordship, expressed by inward remembrance, and witnessing one's servile lowliness, expressed by entreaty; movement between them resembles descent and ascent on a spiritual ascent.
rows.anchor: كمال حال الإنسان إنما يحصل بانكشاف أمرين : أحدهما : عزة الربوبية ، وهذا المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to why these are separately commanded is that knowledge does not always entail humility and fear: someone may reason that God will not punish because punishment harms another without benefiting Him.
rows.anchor: المعرفة لا يلزمها التضرع والخوف على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer distinguishes fear of punishment, characteristic of beginners, from fear of divine majesty, characteristic of realized knowers and intensified by greater knowledge.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عنه بأن الخوف على قسمين : الأول : خوف العقاب ، وهو مقام المبتدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further answer says those granted unveilings experience both beauty and majesty: beauty sustains them, majesty overwhelms them, so remembrance must honor both aspects.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عن هذا الجواب بأن لأصحاب المكاشفات مقامين : مكاشفة الجمال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: An alternate reading has khafiyah; al-Zajjāj derives it from khawfah, with wāw changed to yāʾ because the preceding letter is kasra.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أخرى { وخفية } وقال الزجاج : أصلها ( خوفة ) فقلبت الواو ياء لانكسار ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear may be fear of shortcomings in one's deeds, fear of one's final outcome, or fear that deficient obedience and remembrance cannot repay God's limitless blessings.
rows.anchor: أحدها : خوف التقصير في الأعمال . وثانيها : خوف الخاتمة . والمحققون خوفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The realized fear the prior divine decree, since what was settled beforehand only becomes apparent at the end.
rows.anchor: والمحققون خوفهم من السابقة ، لأنه إنما يظهر في الخاتمة ما سبق الحكم به

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophetic saying 'the pen has dried concerning what will occur until Resurrection Day' supports fear of the prior decree.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كان عليه السلام يقول : ( جف القلم بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة )

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Wāsiṭī says gratitude is shirk; Rāzī suggests he means that claiming to repay God's gifts with thanks makes the servant seem an independent giver, whereas humble gratitude reveals servitude.
rows.anchor: وكان الشيخ أبو بكر الواسطي يقول : الشكر شرك ، فسألوني عن هذه الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the khafiyah reading, beginners conceal remembrance to protect worship from showing off, while the perfected conceal it out of the protective jealousy produced by complete love and absorption.
rows.anchor: وأما القراءة الثانية : وهو قوله : { وخفية } فالإخفاء في حق المبتدين يراد لصون الطاعات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Rāzī supports the perfected person's hidden remembrance with a Prophetic saying that whoever knows God has his tongue fall silent.
rows.anchor: بناء على قوله عليه السلام : ( من عرف الله كل لسانه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance should be at a moderate volume between loudness and whispering, like the instruction for prayer at 17:110 and Zechariah's quiet call at 19:3.
rows.anchor: والمراد منه أن يقع ذلك الذكر بحيث يكون متوسطا بين الجهر والمخافتة كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this means remembering the Lord at a volume one can hear oneself; vocal remembrance affects imagination and thereby strengthens inward spiritual remembrance in a reinforcing cycle.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : وتفسير قوله : { ودون الجهر من القول } المعنى أن يذكر ربه على وجه يسمع نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis treats ghudū as the verbal noun of ghadā, later used for the time of morning departure, as in 'its morning course is a month' at 34:12.
rows.anchor: أنه مصدر يقال غدوت أغدو غدوا غدوا ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { غدوها شهر } ( سبأ : 12 )

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth gives a second analysis: ghudū is the plural of ghudwah, meaning mornings.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : الغدو جمع مثل الغدوات وواحد الغدوات غدوة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the singular of āṣāl is aṣl and the singular of aṣl is aṣīl; muʾṣilīn means arriving at the late-afternoon time.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء : واحدها أصل وواحد الأصل الأصيل . قال يقال جئناهم مؤصلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣīl is linked to aṣl, the beginning: the day with its night is treated as beginning at night, and day's end adjoins the next night's beginning.
rows.anchor: ويقال الأصيل مأخوذ من الأصل واليوم بليلته ، إنما يبتدأ بالشروع من أول الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning turns people from sleep like death to waking like life and the world from darkness to light; evening reverses the change. These striking transitions display God's wisdom and boundless power, warranting remembrance at both times.
rows.anchor: عند الغدوة انقلب الإنسان من النوم الذي هو كالموت إلى اليقظة التي هي كالحياة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view takes morning and evening to signify remembrance as continuously as possible; Ibn ʿAbbās says God would have commanded remembrance in any fourth human posture beyond standing, sitting, and lying down.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال في قوله : { الالباب الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two named times imply remembrance throughout all times, and the final command calls for constant inward awareness of God's majesty and greatness, without a moment of heedlessness insofar as human capacity allows.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ولا تكن من الغافلين } يدل على أن الذكر القلبي يجب أن يكون دائما ، وأن لا يغفل الإنسان لحظة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Soul and body affect each other: imagining sourness makes the teeth ache and imagining an upsetting state heats the body, while repeated bodily action forms a strong, lasting disposition in the soul.
rows.anchor: لأن كل أثر حصل في جوهر الروح نزل منه أثر إلى البدن ، وكل حالة حصلت في البدن صعدت منها نتائج إلى الروح
